content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the structure and blood supply of the liver
Explain the role of the liver in excretion
Describe deamination and the ornithine cycle
Explain other functions of the liver

is a vital organ with many functions, including a key role in excretion. It produces urea from excess amino acids through a process called deamination. The liver also detoxifies harmful substances and stores important nutrients.
Portal vein brings blood directly from intestines
Liver processes before reaching rest of body
Converts excess amino acids to urea
Stores vitamins A, D, B12, iron
Removal of the amino group from amino acids
Used in respiration OR converted to fat
Convert toxic ammonia to less toxic urea
Excess amino acids deaminated in liver
Urea filtered and excreted in urine
Broken down when no longer needed
Can regrow from as little as 25%
The liver makes urea; kidneys excrete it
The liver only has one blood supply
Two supplies: hepatic artery and hepatic portal vein
Liver breaks it down through detoxification
Amino acids are stored for later use
Excess amino acids are deaminated (cannot be stored)
Vessel bringing blood from intestines to liver
Removal of amino group from amino acids
Scarring of liver due to damage
Liver has dual blood supply: hepatic artery and hepatic portal vein
Main excretory role: making urea from excess amino acids
Ornithine cycle converts ammonia to urea (less toxic)
Urea transported to kidneys for excretion
Other functions: detoxification, bile production, glycogen storage, protein synthesis
Alcohol and drugs detoxified in liver
Liver disease impairs these functions; can be life-threatening
